BAYLOR UNIVERSITY

APPLIED PERFORMANCE

Testing Protocol

Testing can be performed under the following conditions.

Condition 1: Performing tests within a training session

Warm up: Team training warm up

Condition 2: Performing tests outside of a training session

Standard Warm up:

Line hops (Forward/Backward/Left/Right) x 10 each

Open gate/Close gate (Hip internal/external rotation) x 5 each

Rapid Squat to Stand (Triple Extension) x 5 each

Testing Order:

Test Protocol/Procedure:

Hands Free Body Weight Squat:

Starting position:

standing posture.

Arms extended out from the shoulder keeping them fixed for each rep.

Feet shoulder width apart.

ForceDecks protocol:

Ask individual to assume starting position.

Weigh individual – Click “Weigh Athlete”. The individual must remain completely still, and the color display must register green before accepting body weight.

Stabilize individual – Instruct the individual to remain completely still, for 2-3 seconds before, and between each rep.

Start recording – Click “Start Recording”.

Perform squat rep then resume the starting position.

Repeat squat for desired number of reps.

Stop recording – Click “Stop Recording”.

Analyze – Click “Analyze and Save”.

Squat Jump:

Starting position:

Partial squat position / quarter-squat position.

Hands on hips.

Chest up and looking forward.

ForceDecks protocol:

Assume starting position – Ask individual to assume starting position.

Weigh individual – Click “Weigh Athlete”. The individual must remain completely still, and the color display must register green before accepting body weight.

Start recording – Click “Start Recording”.

Perform jump - Instruct the individual to:

Lower into a squat position above parallel depth.

Hold position, keeping chest up and hands on hips, for 3 seconds.

Jump up.

Land softly.

Assume starting position again.

Repeat jump for desired number of reps.

Stop recording – Click “Stop Recording”.

Analyze – Click “Analyze and Save”.

Countermovement Jump

Starting position:

Normal standing posture.

Hands on hips (if unweighted) or hands on barbell (if weighted).

Chest up and looking forward.

ForceDecks protocol:

Assume starting position – Ask the individual to assume starting position on the plates.

Weigh individual – Click “Weigh Athlete”. The individual must remain completely still, and the color display must register green before accepting body weight

Start recording – Click “Start Recording”.

Perform jump – Instruct the individual to:

Keep the chest up and looking forward.

Bend down.

Jump up.

Land softly.

Assume starting position again.

Repeat jump total of 3 countermovement jumps.

Stop recording – Click “Stop Recording”.

Analyze – Click “Analyze and Save”.

Hop Test (Repeated CMJ Test)

Starting position:

Normal standing posture.

Hands on hips.

Chest up and looking forward.

ForceDecks protocol:

Assume starting position – Ask individual to assume starting position.

Weigh individual – Click “Weigh Athlete”. The individual must remain completely still, and the color display must register green before accepting body weight.

Stabilize individual – Instruct the athlete/client to remain completely still, in the standing position for 2-3 seconds before the first jump.

Start recording – Click “Start Recording”.

Perform jump – Instruct the individual to:

Keep chest up and looking forward.

Bend down.

Jump up.

Land stiff-legged on only the toes.

Quickly jump off the toes, for the desired number of reps, in rapid succession (safely keeping the knees as straight as possible).

Stop recording – Click “Stop Recording”.

Analyze – Click “Analyze and Save”.

Single Leg Countermovement Jump

Starting position:

Normal standing posture.

Hands on hips (if unweighted) or hands on barbell (if weighted).

Chest up and looking forward.

ForceDecks protocol:

Starting position – Ask the individual to assume starting position on the plates.

Weigh individual – Click “Weigh Athlete”. The individual must remain completely still, and the color display must register green before accepting body weight

Start recording – Click “Start Recording”.

Perform single leg jump – Instruct the individual to:

Keep the chest up and looking forward.

Bend down using only the desired leg for testing.

Jump up using only the desired leg for testing.

Land softly using only the desired leg for testing.

Assume starting position again.

Repeat jump for a total of 3 countermovement jumps each, per leg.

Stop recording – Click “Stop Recording”.

Analyze – Click “Analyze and Save”.

Isometric Seated Calf Raise:

Starting position:

Assume a seated position.

Feet flat at the approximate center of the platform.

Ankle directly under the knee (90 deg position at the knee and ankle).

Place belt/strap approximately a palm width away from the top of the knee.

ForceDecks protocol:

Select “Mid-Thigh Pull” from exercise testing menu.

Weigh individual – Click “Weigh Athlete”. The individual must remain completely still, and the color display must register green before accepting body weight.

Ask individual to assume starting position as described above.

Make sure there is pre-tension through the ankle.

Once belt/strap is in place, no more than a fingertip should fit under.

Start recording – Click “Start Recording”.

Instruct individual to:

Drive maximally with the ball of the foot into the platform.

Maintain contraction for 6 seconds or when instructed to “relax”.

Rest for 15 seconds between reps.

Perform 3 maximal contraction reps.

Stop recording – Click “Stop Recording”.

Analyze – Click “Analyze and Save”.

Technical Definitions
   •   Absolute – the magnitude of a given value (irrespective of being positive or negative)
   •   Acceleration – rate of change in velocity over time of the centre of mass (m/s2)
   •   Asymmetry – a relative measurement of difference between two sided values expressed as a percentage.
       Calculated as (Left Metric value – Right Metric value) / maximum of (Left Metric value or Right Metric value) x 100
   •   Body Mass (BM) – measure of mass collected during weighing (kg)
   •   Body Weight (BW) – mass captured during the ‘Weigh Profile’ stage (N)
   •   Center of Mass (CoM) – the balance point of the body that mass is distributed about
   •   Displacement/Height – change in the vertical position of the Centre of Mass
   •   Force – strength as an attribute of physical action or movement
   •   Impulse (Absolute Impulse) – integration (area under the curve) of Force over a given period time period (Ns)
   •   Impulse (Net Impulse) – area under the force curve over a given time period but only above body weight (Ns)
   •   Impulse (Positive Impulse) – area under the curve from the start of movement to take off (i.e.: eccentric and
       concentric phases combined) but only above body weight (Ns)
   •   Left Force – the vertical Force component measured from the left force plate (N)
   •   Left Metric – metric calculated using only the Left Force
   •   Maximum/Peak – the highest or largest value within a dataset or phase
   •   Mean – average of all data points within a dataset or phase, including the start and end of the phase
   •   Minimum – the single lowest value within a dataset or phase
   •   Power – the work rate a force exerts on an object, calculated as force x velocity (W)
   •   Recording – an entire force-time dataset from the time Start Recording is clicked until Stop Recording is clicked
   •   Rep – short for repetition, a period of time in a recording during which a single instance of a test is performed
   •   Rate of Force Development (RFD) - Change in force over a given time period or phase (N/s)
   •   Right Force – the vertical Force component measured from the right force plate (N)
   •   Right Metric – metric calculated using only the Right Force
   •   Rate of Power Development (RPD) – change in power over a given time period or phase (W/s)
   •   Velocity – change in center of mass position over time (m/s)
   •   Vertical Force – the vertical force component measured from a single force plate or combined from both (N)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cut the two Baylor sources into labeled sections. Stdlib only.

    python digest_check/sources.py

Inputs (all under private/, which is gitignored):
  playbook_raw.txt  `pdftotext -layout` of the May 2024 Operations Guide PDF
                    (~/DEV/Performance_Playbook/Baylor Applied Performance Playbook.pdf)
  v3_flint.md       the Flint text copy of "Revised Force Plate Testing V3.docx",
                    fetched from Drive by id with gws (never the FUSE mount)
  v3.docx           the docx itself, used only to cross-check the word count

Output: private/sections.json, {"A": [...], "B": [...]}, each section {id, title, text}.

Which parts of each source are kept is a decision, written here so it can be argued with:

  A, Operations Guide: the technology overview table, the ForceDecks workflow
    (Prior to Testing / Starting a Test / Recording a Test), the VALD technical
    definitions, and the ForceDecks take-off and landing metric glossary. NOT the Perch
    "Types of Jumping" section: its RSIMod is jump height over time to takeoff, a
    different vendor's definition, and would read as a false contradiction. NOT the
    DynaMo, ForceFrame or NordBord workflows: other devices.
  B, V3 protocol: the preamble (testing conditions and warm-ups) and the Countermovement
    Jump section only. The squat jump, hop test and single-leg sections share the same
    button vocabulary, so keyword matching would route a CMJ claim to, say, the hop
    test's "land stiff-legged" and call the chapter supported when the CMJ section says
    "land softly". The chapter is the CMJ procedure; the CMJ section is the passage.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PRIVATE = HERE / "private"
CAP = 3000  # characters per section sent to Jev


def between(lines: list[str], start: str, end: str, occurrence: int = 1) -> list[str]:
    """Lines from the `occurrence`-th line matching `start` up to (not incl.) `end`."""
    hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if re.search(start, l)]
    if len(hits) < occurrence:
        raise SystemExit(f"anchor not found: {start!r} (occurrence {occurrence})")
    i = hits[occurrence - 1]
    for j in range(i + 1, len(lines)):
        if re.search(end, lines[j]):
            return lines[i:j]
    raise SystemExit(f"end anchor not found after {start!r}: {end!r}")


def tidy(lines: list[str]) -> str:
    """Collapse pdftotext layout spacing; drop page-number-only lines."""
    out = []
    for l in lines:
        s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", l).strip()
        if not s or re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,2}", s):
            continue
        out.append(s)
    return "\n".join(out)


def chunk(title: str, text: str, sid: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Split a long section on line boundaries into pieces under CAP."""
    pieces, cur = [], []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if cur and len("\n".join(cur + [line])) > CAP - 100:
            pieces.append("\n".join(cur))
            cur = []
        cur.append(line)
    if cur:
        pieces.append("\n".join(cur))
    if len(pieces) == 1:
        return [{"id": sid, "title": title, "text": pieces[0]}]
    return [{"id": f"{sid}{k + 1}", "title": f"{title} (part {k + 1} of {len(pieces)})",
             "text": p} for k, p in enumerate(pieces)]


def source_a() -> list[dict]:
    lines = (PRIVATE / "playbook_raw.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    secs = []
    secs += chunk("Operations Guide: Technology overview",
                  tidy(between(lines, r"TECHNOLOGY OVERVIEW", r"LOGIN INFORMATION")), "A_tech")
    fd = between(lines, r"^\s*Prior to Testing\s*$", r"complete list of ForceDecks testing protocols")
    secs += chunk("Operations Guide: ForceDecks workflow", tidy(fd), "A_fd")
    secs += chunk("Operations Guide: VALD technical definitions",
                  tidy(between(lines, r"^Technical Definitions\s*$", r"^Take-Off Phase Metrics", 2)),
                  "A_defs")
    secs += chunk("Operations Guide: ForceDecks jump metric glossary",
                  tidy(between(lines, r"^Take-Off Phase Metrics", r"To access the ForceFrame user guide")),
                  "A_metrics")
    return secs


def source_b() -> list[dict]:
    raw = (PRIVATE / "v3_flint.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    raw = re.sub(r"\A---.*?---\s*", "", raw, flags=re.S)  # Flint's YAML header
    lines = [l.strip() for l in raw.splitlines() if l.strip()]
    pre_end = lines.index("Testing Order:")
    cmj_start = lines.index("Countermovement Jump")
    cmj_end = lines.index("Hop Test (Repeated CMJ Test)")
    pre = "\n".join(lines[:pre_end])
    cmj = "\n".join(lines[cmj_start:cmj_end])
    text = f"{pre}\n\n{cmj}"
    assert len(text) <= CAP, len(text)
    return [{"id": "B_cmj", "title": "V3 protocol: testing conditions, warm-up, and Countermovement Jump",
             "text": text}]


def docx_words(path: Path) -> int:
    xml = zipfile.ZipFile(path).read("word/document.xml").decode("utf-8")
    xml = re.sub(r"<w:p[ >]", "\n<w:p ", xml)
    return len(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", xml).split())


def main() -> int:
    data = {"A": source_a(), "B": source_b()}
    (PRIVATE / "sections.json").write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False),
                                           encoding="utf-8")
    for k, secs in data.items():
        for s in secs:
            print(f"{k} {s['id']:<10} {len(s['text']):>5} chars  {s['title']}")
    if (PRIVATE / "v3.docx").exists():
        print(f"V3 docx word count {docx_words(PRIVATE / 'v3.docx')} "
              "(Flint copy says 885; the docx count omits table pipes and headings)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic extraction of checkable claims from Digest chapter 1. Stdlib only.

    python digest_check/claims.py            # writes private/claims.json, prints a summary

The chapter is read from git, never from a checkout of the branch:
    git -C ~/DEV/Performance_Playbook show origin/digest-start:docs/digest/ch01_forcedecks_cmj.md

Rules, in order:
  * Only the procedure sections are read: Setup, Preparing the athlete, Testing protocol,
    Data quality checks, Troubleshooting, Data management and export, Teardown and
    storage. The short version, the purpose section, the owner table, contacts, revision
    history and open questions are skipped (summary, metadata, or not procedure).
  * A paragraph becomes one claim per sentence. A list item is one claim (its sentences
    kept together). A table row is one claim: header: cell, for each non-empty cell.
  * Any sentence that touches a [CONFIRM: ...] span is dropped. Sentences are split
    BEFORE that filter, so a paragraph or item keeps its other sentences.
  * Sentences about the document itself ("this chapter", "the handbook chapter") and the
    "Photo to add" line are dropped.
Claim ids are c01, c02, ... in document order, so the same chapter gives the same ids.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import subprocess

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Numbers in the chapter, checked in code. Jev never sees or judges a number.

    python digest_check/numbers.py --selftest     # no API, no source files needed

A numeric fact is (key, value). Keys come from two places:
  * a count followed within two words by a unit: "2 countermovement jumps" -> (jumps, 2),
    "2 to 3 second still pause" -> (seconds, 2-3), "Up to 16 profiles" -> (profiles, 16);
  * named settings and drills: "Sequenced Platform Count: 1", "version 2.1",
    "Line hops ... 10 each".
Number words two..twenty become digits first; "2 to 3" and "2-3" are the same range.

Comparison against one source's text: same key and same value is `match`; same key
with a different value is `mismatch`; key absent is `not_in_source` (a coverage gap,
never a mismatch). A mismatch listed in KNOWN_CHOICES is `known_eric_choice`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys

WORDS = {w: str(i) for i, w in enumerate(
    "zero one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve thirteen "
    "fourteen fifteen sixteen seventeen eighteen nineteen twenty".split())}
MASK_WORDS = [w for w, i in WORDS.items() if int(i) >= 2]

UNITS = {
    r"countermovement jumps?|cmj reps?|jumps?": "jumps",
    r"reps?|repetitions?": "reps",
    r"seconds?|s\b": "seconds",
    r"profiles?": "profiles",
    r"hours?": "hours",
    r"minutes?": "minutes",
    r"trials?": "trials",
}
NAMED = {
    "sequenced_platform_count": r"sequenced platform count\D{0,20}?(\d+)",
    "app_version": r"(?:forcedecks|version)\s+(?:app,?\s+)?(?:version\s+)?(\d+\.\d+)",
    "warmup_line_hops": r"line hops[^\n]{0,60}?(\d+)\s*each",
    "warmup_open_close_gate": r"open gate[^\n]{0,60}?(\d+)\s*each",
    "warmup_rapid_squat": r"rapid squat to stand[^\n]{0,40}?(\d+)",
}
# Eric's deliberate changes against the old protocol, per the 2026-10-06 handoff.
# (key, source) -> (chapter value, source value). Only V3 (B) carries a rep count.
KNOWN_CHOICES = {("jumps", "B"): ("2", "3")}

NUM = r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:-\d+)?"


def normalise(text: str) -> str:
    t = text.lower().replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-")
    t = re.sub(r"\b(" + "|".join(WORDS) + r")\b", lambda m: WORDS[m.group(1)], t)
    t = re.sub(r"\b(\d+)\s*(?:to|-)\s*(\d+)\b", r"\1-\2", t)
    return t


def facts(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    t = normalise(text)
    out = []
    for key, pattern in NAMED.items():
        for m in re.finditer(pattern, t):
            out.append((key, m.group(1)))
    for pattern, key in UNITS.items():
        # A count, then at most two plain words, then the unit.
        for m in re.finditer(rf"(?<![\w.])({NUM})\s+(?:[a-z-]+\s+){{0,2}}?(?:{pattern})(?![a-z])", t):
            out.append((key, m.group(1)))
    # The settings value "1" also reads as a bare count; NAMED owns it.
    seen, uniq = set(), []
    for f in out:
        if f not in seen:
            seen.add(f)
            uniq.append(f)
    return uniq


def compare(claim_text: str, source_text: str, source: str) -> list[dict]:
    """One row per numeric fact in the claim."""
    src = {}
    for key, value in facts(source_text):
        src.setdefault(key, set()).add(value)
    rows = []
    for key, value in facts(claim_text):
        values = src.get(key)
        if not values:
            status = "not_in_source"
        elif value in values:
            status = "match"
        elif KNOWN_CHOICES.get((key, source), (None, None))[0] == value and \
                KNOWN_CHOICES[(key, source)][1] in values:
            status = "known_eric_choice"
        else:
            status = "mismatch"
        rows.append({"key": key, "chapter": value,
                     "source": sorted(values) if values else [], "status": status})
    return rows


def mask(text: str) -> str:
    """What Jev sees: every digit run and number word two..twenty becomes [n]."""
    t = re.sub(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?", "[n]", text)
    return re.sub(r"\b(" + "|".join(MASK_WORDS) + r")\b", "[n]", t, flags=re.I)


def selftest() -> int:
    v3 = ("Repeat jump total of 3 countermovement jumps.\n"
          "Line hops (Forward/Backward/Left/Right) x 10 each\n"
          "Open gate/Close gate (Hip internal/external rotation) x 5 each\n"
          "Rapid Squat to Stand (Triple Extension) x 5 each")
    ops = ("o Platforms > Sequenced Platform Count is set to “1”\n"
           "Repeat rep - Have the individual pause for 2-3 seconds, then repeat. "
           "Up to 16 profiles may be tested before stopping the recording.")
    cases = [
        ("Repeat for a total of 2 countermovement jumps, with the 2 to 3 second still pause between them.",
         v3, "B", {("jumps", "known_eric_choice"), ("seconds", "not_in_source")}),
        ("Repeat for a total of 2 countermovement jumps, with the 2 to 3 second still pause between them.",
         ops, "A", {("jumps", "not_in_source"), ("seconds", "match")}),
        ("Repeat for a total of 4 countermovement jumps.", v3, "B", {("jumps", "mismatch")}),
        ("Up to 16 profiles can be tested in one recording.", ops, "A", {("profiles", "match")}),
        ("Up to 12 profiles can be tested in one recording.", ops, "A", {("profiles", "mismatch")}),
        ("Platforms, Sequenced Platform Count: 1", ops, "A", {("sequenced_platform_count", "match")}),
        ("Platforms, Sequenced Platform Count: 2", ops, "A", {("sequenced_platform_count", "mismatch")}),
        ("Line hops, forward and backward then left and right, 10 each", v3, "B", {("warmup_line_hops", "match")}),
        ("Open gate and close gate (hip internal and external rotation), 5 each", v3, "B",
         {("warmup_open_close_gate", "match")}),
        ("Rapid squat to stand (triple extension), 5", v3, "B", {("warmup_rapid_squat", "match")}),
        ("No food or caffeine in the two hours before a planned test.", v3, "B", {("hours", "not_in_source")}),
        ("New athletes get at least three familiarization trials.", v3, "B", {("trials", "not_in_source")}),
        ("The testing device runs ForceDecks 2.1, the latest release.", ops, "A", {("app_version", "not_in_source")}),
        ("Wipe the plate surfaces.", v3, "B", set()),
    ]
    failures = 0
    for text, src, name, want in cases:
        got = {(r["key"], r["status"]) for r in compare(text, src, name)}
        ok = got == want
        failures += not ok
        print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name} {text[:60]:<62} {sorted(got)}")
    masked = mask("Repeat for a total of 2 countermovement jumps, two hours, ForceDecks 2.1, one foot")
    ok = masked == "Repeat for a total of [n] countermovement jumps, [n] hours, ForceDecks [n], one foot"
    failures += not ok
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] mask: {masked}")
    print(f"\n{len(cases) + 1 - failures} of {len(cases) + 1} cases pass")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(selftest() if "--selftest" in sys.argv else 0)

"""Run the chapter 1 consistency check: numbers in code, prose by Jev. Resumable.

    python digest_check/check.py              # finished pairs in runs/jev.jsonl are skipped

each plant against its target source only:
  1. Passage choice, in code. B is always the V3 preamble plus its CMJ section (see
     sources.py for why). A is the one section with the highest IDF-weighted overlap
     with the claim's words; ties and zero overlap go to the ForceDecks workflow.
  2. Numbers, in code (numbers.py), against the whole kept text of that source.
     Written to runs/numbers.jsonl: ids, keys and values, no source text.
  3. One Jev request with two Nouls. Digits and number words two..twenty are masked
     to [n] in both claim and passage, so Jev cannot judge a number even by accident.
     Raw probabilities go to runs/jev.jsonl: ids and probabilities only.
A pair is flagged when contradiction >= 0.50 and coverage >= 0.50 (report.py).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import math
import re
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent / "zotero_classify"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))

import numbers as numcheck  # noqa: E402  (local numbers.py, shadows the stdlib module on purpose)

PRIVATE = HERE / "private"
RUNS = HERE / "runs"
DEFAULT_A = "A_fd"

STOP = set("""a an the and or of to in on for with by at from as is are be it its this that these
those then than not no if into out up do does each any all your you they them their there when
while before after only per which what who how can may must should will so but also same one
""".split())

QUESTIONS = {
    "contradiction": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": (
            "Use only `source_passage` and `chapter_claim` in the state. Do not use outside "
            "knowledge of ForceDecks, VALD, force plates or testing practice. Numbers are "
            "masked as [n] and are checked elsewhere; ignore them. Question: does "
            "`source_passage` give a different instruction, cue, order of steps, button, "
            "condition, setting or definition for the same step or the same thing that "
            "`chapter_claim` describes? If the passage does not mention that step, answer no."),
        "criteria": {

                      "passage": sec["text"]})
    return pairs


def state_for(pair: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        "chapter_claim": numcheck.mask(pair["text"]),
        "chapter_section": pair["claim_section"],
        "source_name": pair["section_title"],
        "source_passage": numcheck.mask(pair["passage"]),
    }


def ask(pair: dict, key: str) -> dict:
    started = time.monotonic()
    delay = 2.0
    for attempt in range(4):
        try:
            answers = jev_client.system_one(state_for(pair), QUESTIONS, key, timeout=30.0)
            break
        except jev_client.JevError as e:
            transient = any(t in str(e) for t in ("429", "529", "timeout", "URLError"))
            if not transient or attempt == 3:
                raise
            time.sleep(delay)
            delay *= 2
    out = {}
    for name in QUESTIONS:
        a = answers.get(name)
        if not isinstance(a, dict) or not isinstance(a.get("noul"), (int, float)):
            raise jev_client.JevError(f"bad {name} answer: {a!r}")
        out[name] = round(float(a["noul"]), 4)
    return {"pair": pair["pair"], "claim_id": pair["claim_id"], "source": pair["source"],
            "section_id": pair["section_id"], "plant": pair["plant"], **out,
            "attempts": attempt + 1, "ms": int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)}


def write_numbers(sections, pairs) -> None:
    full = {k: "\n".join(s["text"] for s in v) for k, v in sections.items()}
    RUNS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with (RUNS / "numbers.jsonl").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for p in pairs:
            for row in numcheck.compare(p["text"], full[p["source"]], p["source"]):
                fh.write(json.dumps({"pair": p["pair"], "claim_id": p["claim_id"],
                                     "source": p["source"], "plant": p["plant"], **row}) + "\n")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dry", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    sections, claims, plants = load()
    pairs = build_pairs(sections, claims, plants)
    write_numbers(sections, pairs)
    if args.dry:
        print(json.dumps({"state": state_for(pairs[0]), "questions": QUESTIONS}, indent=1)[:3000])
        from collections import Counter
        print(Counter(p["section_id"] for p in pairs if p["source"] == "A"))
        return 0

    out = RUNS / "jev.jsonl"
    done = set()
    if out.exists():
        for line in out.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            try:
                done.add(json.loads(line)["pair"])
            except (ValueError, KeyError):
                continue
    todo = [p for p in pairs if p["pair"] not in done]
    print(f"{len(pairs)} pairs ({len(claims)} claims x 2 sources + {len(plants)} plants), "
          f"{len(done)} done, {len(todo)} to do")
    key = jev_client.api_key()
    failures = []
    started = time.monotonic()
    with out.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh, ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
        def work(p):
            try:
                return p, ask(p, key), None
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                return p, None, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        for p, res, err in pool.map(work, todo):
            if err:
                failures.append((p["pair"], err))
                continue
            fh.write(json.dumps(res) + "\n")
            fh.flush()
    print(f"wall {time.monotonic() - started:.1f}s, failures: {len(failures)}")
    for f in failures[:10]:
        print(" ", *f)
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

                     app versions already explains

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from collections import Counter

    ("2 reps (V3 says 3)", r"\b(2|two) (countermovement|cmj|reps?)", r"\b3\b|\bthree\b"),

    ("data path: VALD Hub to Kitman and the department database by API",

    ("hands on hips", r"hands? on (your )?hips", None),
]

    "c14|B": "The claim describes the two sources. Checked by hand: accurate. V3 does use "
             "Weigh Athlete, Start Recording and Analyze and Save; the Operations Guide "
             "does say Play and Weigh Start. Jev most likely read the V3 passage's silence "
             "on Play and Weigh Start as a conflict. No action.",
    "c37|A": "Button name only: the guide confirms weighing with Weigh Start or Start, "
             "the chapter says Weigh Athlete (V3 name). The chapter's note on app versions "
             "already says this, and its [CONFIRM] to check the names on the 2.1 screens is "
             "the real fix. The green-display rule comes from V3 and is not in the guide.",
}

    ("c44 (with c39, c42, c16)",
     "Testing protocol steps 4 to 9 start and stop a recording for each athlete "
     "(\"repeat from step 1\"), but the Operations Guide records the whole queue in one "
     "recording and stops once, and the chapter's own Build the queue says \"Up to 16 "
     "profiles can be tested in one recording.\" Decide which one the staff do and make "
     "steps 7 to 9 say it.",

     "the recording.",

    wall_ms = sum(r["ms"] for r in jev.values())
    unexplained = [f for f in flags if f["kind"] == "unexplained_contradiction"]
    known = [f for f in flags if f["kind"] == "known_eric_choice"]
    other = [f for f in flags if f["kind"] == "other"]

    L = []
    add = L.append
    add("# Digest chapter 1: consistency check against Baylor's ForceDecks protocols")
    add("")
    add("Run 2026-10-22, before the 2026-10-23 ship. A check, not a pre-registered measurement: no bars.")
    add(f"Chapter: `{check.load.__module__ and 'Performance_Playbook ' + json.loads((HERE / 'private' / 'claims.json').read_text())['ref']}`, "
        f"sha256 `{json.loads((HERE / 'private' / 'claims.json').read_text())['sha256'][:16]}`.")
    add("Sources: A = Operations Guide, May 2024 PDF, ForceDecks text only. "
        "B = Revised Force Plate Testing V3, CMJ section and its warm-up preamble.")
    add(f"{len(claims)} chapter claims x 2 sources = {2 * len(claims)} pairs, plus {len(plants)} plants. "
        f"A pair is flagged when Jev's contradiction and coverage are both at least {FLAG:.2f}.")
    add("")
    add("## 1. Look at these before shipping")
    add("")
    if unexplained:
        for f in unexplained:
            add(f"- **{f['claim_id']} vs {SOURCE_NAME[f['source']]}**, p = {f['p_contradict']:.2f}. "
                f"Chapter: \"{short(f['text'], 140)}\" Source: \"{f['snippet']}\"")
    else:
        add("**Jev found no unexplained contradiction.** Every flagged pair is either one of "
            "your deliberate changes (section 2) or explained below.")
    add("")
    add("One thing found by hand while reading the flags (not a Jev flag):")
    add("")
    for ids, what, src, why in HAND_FINDINGS:
        add(f"- **{ids}: recording per athlete vs one recording per queue.** {what} "
            f"Guide: \"{src}\" {why}")
    add("")
    if other:
        add("Flagged, explained, no action beyond the open [CONFIRM]:")
        add("")
        for f in other:
            add(f"- {f['claim_id']} vs {SOURCE_NAME[f['source']]}, p = {f['p_contradict']:.2f}. "
                f"Chapter: \"{short(f['text'], 100)}\" Source: \"{f['snippet']}\" {f['note']}")
        add("")
    add("## 2. Your deliberate changes (expected, reported separately)")
    add("")
    for f in known:
        add(f"- {f['claim_id']} vs {SOURCE_NAME[f['source']]}, Jev p = {f['p_contradict']:.2f}: "
            f"{f['label']}. Source: \"{f['snippet']}\"")
    for n in num_flags:
        if n["status"] == "known_eric_choice":
            add(f"- {n['claim_id']} vs {SOURCE_NAME[n['source']]}, in code: CMJ count, chapter "
                f"{n['chapter']}, source {', '.join(n['source'] if isinstance(n['source'], list) else [n['source']])}. "
                "2 reps (V3 says 3).")
    add("- Hands on hips: not a change against V3, whose CMJ section already says hands on hips "
        "(unweighted). Nothing flagged.")
    add("- ForceDecks app 2.1: neither source gives a version number (the guide names the app "
        "\"ForceDecks Jump\"). Nothing to compare; the 2.1 line in Equipment sits in a [CONFIRM] and was skipped.")
    add("- Data path to Kitman and the department database by API: the guide calls Kitman the "
        "central data store and says nothing about how data gets there. Not flagged.")
    add("- Missed by Jev: c33, the \"Explain the test\" script (\"Land on both feet in a stiff athletic "
        "position\"), scored 0.42 against V3's \"Land softly\". The same change was caught at c40 and c50.")
    add("")
    add("## 3. Numbers (checked in code, never by Jev)")
    add("")
    real_mismatch = [n for n in num_flags if n["status"] == "mismatch"]
    add(f"- Mismatches: {len(real_mismatch)}." + ("" if real_mismatch else " None."))
    for n in real_mismatch:
        add(f"  - {n['claim_id']} vs {n['source']}: {n['key']} chapter {n['chapter']}, source {n['source']}")
    add(f"- Known choice: 1 (CMJ count 2 vs V3's 3, c41).")
    add("- Agree with a source: " + "; ".join(
        f"{n['claim_id']} {n['key'].replace('_', ' ')} {n['chapter']} ({n['source'][0] if False else SOURCE_NAME[n['source']].split(' (')[0] if isinstance(n['source'], str) else ''})"
        for n in num_match) + ".")
    add("- In no source: " + "; ".join(
        f"{cid} {key.replace('_', ' ')} {val}" for (cid, key, val) in num_absent) +
        ". These are the chapter's own rules or facts, not drift.")
    add("")
    add(f"## 4. Planted contradictions: {caught_n} of {len(plant_res)} caught")
    add("")
    add("Ten altered copies of real chapter claims, each wrong on a non-numeric point against one "
        "source, written to `plants.csv` before any Jev call (sha256 "
        "`3528dec95c1459e1...`). Caught = both Nouls at least 0.50 on the target source.")
    add("")
    add("| Plant | Base | Source | What was changed | Contradiction | Coverage | Caught |")
    add("|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|")
    for pid, pl, r, caught in plant_res:
        add(f"| {pid} | {pl['base_claim_id']} | {pl['target_source']} | {pl['what_changed']} | "
            f"{r['contradiction']:.2f} | {r['coverage']:.2f} | {'yes' if caught else 'no'} |")
    add("")
    add("The plants are blunt (each says the opposite of a source line). Ten of ten says Jev "
        "sees a clear reversal; it does not say Jev sees a quiet one. The per-athlete recording "
        "item in section 1 is the counter-example: stated plainly (p10) it was caught; implied "
        "by step order in the real chapter it was not.")
    add("")
    add(f"## 5. Coverage gaps: {len(gaps)} chapter claims no source addresses")
    add("")
    add("Both coverage Nouls under 0.50. Coverage ran generous (\"Plate cables and power "
        "supply\" scored 0.55), so this list is a floor, not the full set. None of these is "
        "wrong; they are the parts of the chapter that rest on the chapter alone.")
    add("")
    by_sec = {}
    for c, a, b in gaps:
        by_sec.setdefault(c["section"].split(" > ")[0], []).append(c)
    for sec, cs in by_sec.items():
        add(f"- {sec}: " + "; ".join(f"{c['id']} {short(c['text'], 60)}" for c in cs))
    add("")
    add("## 6. Cost and calls")
    add("")
    add(f"- {calls} Jev requests in the recorded run ({2 * len(claims)} claim pairs + {len(plants)} plants), "
        f"two Nouls each, 0 failures, 0 retries. Plus 3 smoke-test requests before the run (not recorded).")
    add(f"- Latency: {wall_ms / 1000:.1f} s summed over requests; 7.5 s wall clock with 4 workers.")
    add("- Credits: not recorded. `jev_client.system_one` returns answers only and drops `usage`; "
        "the shared client was not changed for this.")
    add("")
    add("## 7. Limits")
    add("")
    add("- Source B passage is fixed to the V3 preamble plus its CMJ section. Claims about steps V3 "
        "gives only for other tests (the 2 to 3 second stabilize pause is in V3's squat and hop "
        "sections, not its CMJ section) show as not covered by V3.")
    add("- Source A passage is the guide's ForceDecks workflow plus one keyword-matched section "
        "(technology overview, technical definitions, or a jump-metric glossary chunk). Other "
        "devices' workflows and the Perch jump section were left out on purpose.")
    add("- Sentences touching a [CONFIRM] were skipped, so placeholders are not checked at all, "
        "including the Equipment line with \"version 2.1\" and the Effort and Count rows of the "
        "quality table.")
    add("- Digits and number words were masked to [n] for Jev. A conflict that lives only in a "
        "number goes through the code check, which only knows the units it lists (jumps, reps, "
        "seconds, profiles, hours, minutes, trials, the platform count, the version, the warm-up drills).")
    add("- One Jev run, no repeat runs, so no stability estimate. Thresholds were set at 0.50 by the "
        "task, not tuned.")
    add("- The V3 text is the Flint extraction of the docx, fetched from Drive by id. The docx "
        "itself was downloaded and its word count checked (868 body words vs Flint's 885, which "
        "counts the table).")
    add("- The Operations Guide is the May 2024 PDF. sources.md says the Nov 2025 docx is 97.5% "
        "identical; the docx was not read.")
    add("")
    (HERE / "REPORT.md").write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    summary = {"claims": len(claims), "calls": calls, "flags": flags,
               "num_flags": num_flags, "plants_caught": caught_n, "plants": len(plant_res),
               "gaps": [c["id"] for c, *_ in gaps]}
    (HERE / "runs" / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {**summary, "flags": [{k: v for k, v in f.items() if k not in ("text", "snippet", "note")}
                              for f in flags]}, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({k: (len(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v) for k, v in summary.items()}))
    for f in flags:
        print(f["pair"], f["kind"], f["p_contradict"], "|", f["snippet"])
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

  other              the claim describes the sources themselves, or uses the V3 button
                     names against the Operations Guide, which the chapter's own note on
                     app versions already explains
  unexplained_contradiction   everything else

Source snippets in the report are at most 25 words, picked in code.

]

# Digest chapter 1: consistency check against Baylor's ForceDecks protocols

Run 2026-10-22, before the 2026-10-23 ship. A check, not a pre-registered measurement: no bars.
Chapter: Performance_Playbook `origin/digest-start:docs/digest/ch01_forcedecks_cmj.md`, sha256 `83701c6c4b01f9d7`.
Sources: A = Operations Guide, May 2024 PDF, ForceDecks text only. B = Revised Force Plate Testing V3, CMJ section and its warm-up preamble.
84 chapter claims x 2 sources = 168 pairs, plus 10 plants. A pair is flagged when Jev's contradiction and coverage are both at least 0.50.

## 1. Look at these before shipping

**Jev found no unexplained contradiction.** Every flagged pair is either one of your deliberate changes (section 2) or explained below.

One thing found by hand while reading the flags (not a Jev flag):

- **c44 (with c39, c42, c16): recording per athlete vs one recording per queue.** Testing protocol steps 4 to 9 start and stop a recording for each athlete ("repeat from step 1"), but the Operations Guide records the whole queue in one recording and stops once, and the chapter's own Build the queue says "Up to 16 profiles can be tested in one recording." Decide which one the staff do and make steps 7 to 9 say it. Guide: "Select next individual (profile) ... Up to 16 profiles may be tested before stopping the recording." Jev did not flag the real claims (c44 vs the guide: contradiction 0.07). It did catch plant p10, which states the per-athlete rule outright (0.93).

Flagged, explained, no action beyond the open [CONFIRM]:

- c14 vs V3 protocol, p = 0.69. Chapter: "The Operations Guide describes buttons called Weigh Start and Play; the V3 protocol describes Wei..." Source: "Weigh individual – Click “Weigh Athlete”. The individual must remain completely still, and the color display must register green before accepting body weight" The claim describes the two sources. Checked by hand: accurate. V3 does use Weigh Athlete, Start Recording and Analyze and Save; the Operations Guide does say Play and Weigh Start. Jev most likely read the V3 passage's silence on Play and Weigh Start as a conflict. No action.
- c37 vs Operations Guide (May 2024 PDF), p = 0.63. Chapter: "Weigh. Click Weigh Athlete. The athlete must be completely still. Do not accept body weight until..." Source: "Body Weight (BW) – mass captured during the ‘Weigh Profile’ stage (N)" Button name only: the guide confirms weighing with Weigh Start or Start, the chapter says Weigh Athlete (V3 name). The chapter's note on app versions already says this, and its [CONFIRM] to check the names on the 2.1 screens is the real fix. The green-display rule comes from V3 and is not in the guide.

## 2. Your deliberate changes (expected, reported separately)

- c50 vs V3 protocol, Jev p = 0.93: stiff athletic landing (V3 says land softly). Source: "Land softly."
- c40 vs V3 protocol, Jev p = 0.91: stiff athletic landing (V3 says land softly). Source: "Land softly."
- c41 vs V3 protocol, in code: CMJ count, chapter 2, source 3. 2 reps (V3 says 3).
- Hands on hips: not a change against V3, whose CMJ section already says hands on hips (unweighted). Nothing flagged.
- ForceDecks app 2.1: neither source gives a version number (the guide names the app "ForceDecks Jump"). Nothing to compare; the 2.1 line in Equipment sits in a [CONFIRM] and was skipped.
- Data path to Kitman and the department database by API: the guide calls Kitman the central data store and says nothing about how data gets there. Not flagged.
- Missed by Jev: c33, the "Explain the test" script ("Land on both feet in a stiff athletic position"), scored 0.42 against V3's "Land softly". The same change was caught at c40 and c50.

## 3. Numbers (checked in code, never by Jev)

- Mismatches: 0. None.
- Known choice: 1 (CMJ count 2 vs V3's 3, c41).
- Agree with a source: c11 sequenced platform count 1 (guide); c16 profiles 16 (guide); c21 warmup line hops 10 (V3); c22 warmup open close gate 5 (V3); c23 warmup rapid squat 5 (V3); c38 seconds 2-3 (guide); c41 seconds 2-3 (guide).
- In no source: c13 app version 2.1; c27 hours 2; c28 hours 48; c30 trials 3. These are the chapter's own rules or facts, not drift.

## 4. Planted contradictions: 10 of 10 caught

Ten altered copies of real chapter claims, each wrong on a non-numeric point against one source, written to `plants.csv` before any Jev call (sha256 `3528dec95c1459e1...`). Caught = both Nouls at least 0.50 on the target source.

| Plant | Base | Source | What was changed | Contradiction | Coverage | Caught |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| p01 | c37 | B | condition: V3 says completely still and accept only when the display registers green | 0.98 | 0.98 | yes |
| p02 | c39 | B | order: V3 weighs the athlete, then clicks Start Recording | 0.97 | 0.98 | yes |
| p03 | c36 | B | cue: V3 says hands on hips if unweighted | 0.86 | 0.97 | yes |

| p08 | c17 | A | condition: Ops Guide says ensure nothing is touching the plates before they zero | 0.83 | 0.93 | yes |
| p09 | c55 | A | formula: Ops Guide says (left minus right) divided by the maximum of left or right | 0.97 | 0.98 | yes |
| p10 | c16 | A | condition: Ops Guide says up to 16 profiles may be tested before stopping the recording | 0.93 | 0.98 | yes |

The plants are blunt (each says the opposite of a source line). Ten of ten says Jev sees a clear reversal; it does not say Jev sees a quiet one. The per-athlete recording item in section 1 is the counter-example: stated plainly (p10) it was caught; implied by step order in the real chapter it was not.

## 5. Coverage gaps: 12 chapter claims no source addresses

Both coverage Nouls under 0.50. Coverage ran generous ("Plate cables and power supply" scored 0.55), so this list is a floor, not the full set. None of these is wrong; they are the parts of the chapter that rest on the chapter alone.

- Setup: c06 Credentials are in the vault, not in this document.
- Preparing the athlete: c26 Same time of day as the athlete's previous tests, within...; c27 No food or caffeine in the two hours before a planned test.; c29 Shoes: the same type the athlete trained in last time. No...; c35 The strategy is what we are measuring.
- Troubleshooting: c65 Do not share athlete data in a support ticket; describe t...
- Data management and export: c70 File naming for any manual export follows the SOP templat...; c71 Use the athlete ID, not the name, in file names.
- Teardown and storage: c81 Power down the plates and the device.; c82 Disconnect cables; coil, do not bend at the connector.; c83 Wipe the plate surfaces.; c84 Put the device on charge.

## 6. Cost and calls

- 178 Jev requests in the recorded run (168 claim pairs + 10 plants), two Nouls each, 0 failures, 0 retries. Plus 3 smoke-test requests before the run (not recorded).
- Latency: 29.6 s summed over requests; 7.5 s wall clock with 4 workers.
- Credits: not recorded. `jev_client.system_one` returns answers only and drops `usage`; the shared client was not changed for this.

## 7. Limits

- Source B passage is fixed to the V3 preamble plus its CMJ section. Claims about steps V3 gives only for other tests (the 2 to 3 second stabilize pause is in V3's squat and hop sections, not its CMJ section) show as not covered by V3.
- Source A passage is the guide's ForceDecks workflow plus one keyword-matched section (technology overview, technical definitions, or a jump-metric glossary chunk). Other devices' workflows and the Perch jump section were left out on purpose.
- Sentences touching a [CONFIRM] were skipped, so placeholders are not checked at all, including the Equipment line with "version 2.1" and the Effort and Count rows of the quality table.
- Digits and number words were masked to [n] for Jev. A conflict that lives only in a number goes through the code check, which only knows the units it lists (jumps, reps, seconds, profiles, hours, minutes, trials, the platform count, the version, the warm-up drills).
- One Jev run, no repeat runs, so no stability estimate. Thresholds were set at 0.50 by the task, not tuned.
- The V3 text is the Flint extraction of the docx, fetched from Drive by id. The docx itself was downloaded and its word count checked (868 body words vs Flint's 885, which counts the table).
- The Operations Guide is the May 2024 PDF. sources.md says the Nov 2025 docx is 97.5% identical; the docx was not read.

# Digest check: chapter 1 against Baylor's ForceDecks protocols

Built and run 2026-10-22, the day before Applied Performance Digest chapter 1 (ForceDecks CMJ
procedure) ships on 2026-10-23. This is a consistency **check**, not a pre-registered
measurement: there are no pass bars. Findings are in `REPORT.md`.

What it asks, for every procedural claim in the chapter and each of two Baylor sources:
does the source give a different instruction for the same step, and does it address the
step at all? Numbers are compared in code; Jev only judges prose and never sees a digit.

## Sources

| Id | Source | Where the text came from |
